description: Hi! I’m a high school student from Thailand interested in space, physics, and Earth science. I’m developing EARTHSONA, a website that turns Earth data into sound and stories. I’m looking for teammates interested in coding, data science, sound design, or UI/UX. You don’t need to be an expert, just curious and willing to learn. Let’s create something meaningful together!
summary:
EARTHSONA is an interactive web-based project that explores how Earth science data can be transformed into musical experiences through data sonification. It focuses on making complex environmental and planetary information easier to explore and experience through sound rather than relying only on visual charts and maps.
The project presents selected Earth science themes, including nighttime lights, ocean conditions, atmospheric aerosols, air quality, global carbon dioxide, lightning, and forest height. Users can generate and listen to sound compositions, control individual sound layers, and download the generated audio as a WAV file.
EARTHSONA aims to create a new way of experiencing our planet by connecting scientific information with music. It encourages people, especially those who may find scientific datasets difficult to understand, to explore Earth’s changing systems through an accessible and creative form of storytelling.
details:
EARTHSONA is a web-based data sonification prototype that explores the relationship between Earth science and sound. It transforms predefined data-inspired sound profiles into musical compositions using programmed sound generation.

The website allows users to select an Earth science theme, generate a composition, play or stop the audio, adjust individual sound layers, and download the generated result as a WAV file. It also supports single-layer and dual-layer compositions, allowing different sound elements to be experienced together.

The project uses JavaScript and the Web Audio API to generate sounds directly in the browser. Its sound engine uses programmed rules to control musical elements such as pitch, rhythm, and sound layers. It does not use AI-generated music or prerecorded songs.

The creative idea behind EARTHSONA is to present Earth science through an alternative sensory experience. Instead of only displaying scientific information through numbers, maps, or images, the project explores how data-inspired musical structures can communicate the character of different Earth systems.

During development, we considered accessibility, ease of use, the relationship between sound and scientific themes, and the ability to explore multiple environmental topics through one website.

The current version is a working prototype using predefined, deterministic test sound profiles. It is not yet directly connected to live NASA datasets. Its purpose is to demonstrate the concept and establish a foundation for future development of data-driven sonification.
